To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Asian American students were more likely to experience psychological distress than Caucasian students, and that the relationship between outcome expectancies, affectivity, pessimism, and psychological distress differed between Asian and Caucasian students.

(a) Asian and Caucasian Americans differed in their levels of psychological disturbance, pessimism, and affectivity, (b) pessimism was associated with higher levels of psychological distress, and (c) pessimism was indirectly associated with psychological disturbance via its association with negative affectivity.
Asian Americans reported more pessimism, more negative affectivity, and more psychological distress than Caucasians.

the role of outcome expectations and affectivity in psychological disturbance in two ethnic groups of American college students.
